inventory.label: the heron feather
inventory.notes: Mira saw the feather today and did not write *heron feather* in her ledger again. She wrote *the squirrel who reads.* The feather is still on his back; its meaning has shifted on the public record.

inventory.label: a single rust-colored kit-tuft
inventory.notes: Still on the kitchen ledge. Mira asked to see it; YY showed her; she did not ask for it. He kept it.

inventory.label: a strip of dried apple
inventory.notes: Mira's ledger entry-fee. Half eaten on the path; half rolled into a coil and tucked into a knot in the kitchen wall.

identity_notes: Late winter — YY ate half the apple-strip on the path; the other half is in the kitchen-knot. Food coming up off the floor.
Yesterday: read the fox's exit trail and found one hickory kernel.

Today: Mira asked what he had been reading; he told her — the deer at the surge, the fox at the scratch-pine, the kit-tuft at the den. She wrote *the squirrel who reads* in her ledger and gave him a dried apple-strip in trade.
Standing thread: the feather's public meaning has shifted from heron-token to reader-mark. The feather no longer travels alone on the ledger; it travels as part of YY's role.
